Priya (support): heads-up: ACME reported a sharp p99 jump this morning around 09:50 UTC. Only affects short prompts (<80 tokens) on their dedicated cluster. p50 looks normal. Customer is seeing timeouts and slow UI. Request ids: req_ajk2, req_bk33, req_ck99. Linking logs: https://logs.internal/acme/req_ajk2

infra-bot: deploy/rollout completed at 2026-03-15T09:42:11Z by @alex. Change: continuous-batcher hold_ms increased 8 -> 60 as part of throughput-tune-2026-03-15.

Alex Chen: ack. @Priya can you share a couple of example requests and which route they hit? Is this only ACME?

Priya (support): examples above are on route=acme-chat, model=rwd-3b-quant. Customer says it started right after the morning deploy. Only small prompts (single-line system+user). Not seeing errors for larger prompts.

Jordan (sre): pulled metrics from prod. Quick summary: overall tokens/sec up ~12%, throughput good, but p95/p99 for request_latency_ms on route=acme-chat jumped from ~110ms to ~780ms p99 during the window. Size bucket breakdown: small(<80 tokens) accounts for 62% of requests but only 18% of tokens. Logs show many small requests waiting for batch fill. Query used: 
```
sum(rate(requests_total{route="acme-chat"}[5m])) by (size_bucket)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{route="acme-chat"}[5m])) by (le))
```
Jordan (sre): also noticed increased variance in inter-arrival for some customer flows (bursty web UI). With hold_ms=60, small requests often wait close to the full hold window before being released, causing the tail.

Maria Patel: this is the classic hold-vs-size tradeoff. Increasing hold reduces wasted kernels and improves throughput for long prompts, but for tiny prompt workloads it increases tail. There are a few mitigations we typically consider: 
- per-route hold_ms (lower for low-latency routes)
- fast-path for tiny requests: if token_count <= 64, bypass batching or use immediate-release path
- max-batch-delay adaptive: adjust hold based on observed inter-arrival percentiles (e.g., target 90th inter-arrival < hold)
- jitter/coalesce-timeout smoothing to avoid synchronized releases

Maria Patel: quick note: KV cache warmup isn't the issue here (these are short contexts). This is pure batching hold time causing head-of-line waits.

Priya (support): customer is pushing for quick fix. Can we roll back the hold change or apply per-route override?

Alex Chen: propose immediate mitigation: roll per-route override for route=acme-chat to hold_ms=10 and enable tiny-request fast-path. I'll run a targeted rollout. If that moves p99 down we can keep and iterate.

Alex Chen: command I plan to run: 
```
redwoodctl rollout batcher-config --set hold_ms=10 --route acme-chat --set tiny_fastpath=true --reason "hotfix: acme small-prompt p99"
```

infra-bot: rollout started: batcher-config (route=acme-chat) -> hold_ms=10, tiny_fastpath=true. Rollout id: r-20260315-17. Monitoring for 15m.

oncall-luca: pinging alerting: created a temporary alert suppression for noisy flaps on this route during rollback window.

Jordan (sre): preliminary stats 5m after rollout id r-20260315-17: p99 dropped from ~780ms -> ~210ms, p95 -> 95ms. Request rate steady. Looks promising.

Priya (support): forwarded to ACME: they report UI latency improved and fewer timeouts. They asked why change caused this — can we explain before we close?

Maria Patel: short explainer you can share: we increased batch hold to reduce kernel invocations for efficiency (better throughput for long-running/large requests). For high-frequency small requests that makes them wait longer for a batch to fill, which increases tail latency. We rolled a per-route override and a fast-path to keep small requests latencies low while preserving throughput for other workloads.

Alex Chen: longer-term action items we agreed on: 
- implement adaptive hold algorithm prototype (owner: Maria, due EOW)
- add per-route default policy with low-latency tag and fast-path toggle (owner: Jordan, PR in 2 days)
- add dashboard for small-request fraction and p99 correlation (owner: Alex, quick grafana panel)
- write runbook entry: when increasing hold_ms, check small-request ratio and inter-arrival percentiles (owner: Priya)

Jordan (sre): PR for quick mitigate (per-route fast-path flag) opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/batcher/pulls/2123. CI green. Staging tested with simulated tiny-request bursts.
